title: Mutinous imperial troops sack Rome
summary: Unpaid soldiers of Charles V, including German Landsknechte, stormed Rome, killed thousands and looted the city while Pope Clement VII hid in Castel Sant'Angelo.
reason: Clement VII had joined the League of Cognac against Charles V, and the emperor's army in Italy had gone unpaid and out of control.
significance: It is often seen as the end of the High Renaissance in Rome and left the papacy under imperial influence.
